themes.name: Self-efficacy measurement
themes.definition: Studies focused on developing, adapting, or validating instruments to measure engineering students' self-efficacy beliefs in various domains such as general engineering, programming, design, or basic electronics skills.
evidence: [2DDA52FC] Two scales for engineering self-efficacy have recently been developed for undergraduate students, with validity evidence relating self-efficacy responses to persistence and achievement in engineering.

[J4L96ZTQ] This study evaluates the factor structure, validity, and reliability of general and skill-specific engineering self-efficacy measures created for use with undergraduate engineering students.
[Y345N2W5] The aim of this study is to improve a measurement tool to evaluate the self-efficacy of Electrical-Electronics Engineering students through their basic electronics skills.

themes.name: Scale validation and psychometric properties
themes.definition: Research that employs factor analysis (exploratory and confirmatory), reliability coefficients (e.g., Cronbach's alpha), and other psychometric methods to establish the validity and reliability of measurement instruments for engineering education constructs.
evidence: [CY59SPDS] We calculated the reliability index of the instruments for the extent to which the measurements are repeatable, and the item discrimination index for the extent to which the items can distinguish highly motivated students from poorly motivated ones.

[49BIH9AZ] The findings of EFA resulted in ten factors of employability. Subsequently, CFA identified nine different factors: leadership, critical thinking, numeracy, sociability, using technology, planning and organizing, problem-solving, teamwork, and emotional intelligence skills.

[DFVK7NR2] Exploratory factor analysis resulted in four factors: clear goals, workplace support, university support, and generic competencies. Confirmatory factor analyses demonstrated that the correlated four-factor model provided an acceptable fit with the data.

themes.name: Employability and professional skills assessment
themes.definition: Studies that develop or validate instruments to measure employability skills, professional competencies, or workplace-related skills (e.g., communication, teamwork, problem-solving) in engineering students, often linking these to industry requirements.
evidence: [LHGYXXJG] The study aims to identify indicators that can measure students' employability skills and attributes. The research model, based on The Conference Board of Canada (Employability Skills 2000+), is divided into fundamental skills, personal management skills, and cooperative skills.
[49BIH9AZ] The purpose of this study is to identify employability skills among aspiring engineering graduates and develop measurement scale to assess their skill sets.

[4I9HTBU4] This study aimed to develop a valid and reliable survey instrument to measure Workplace Oral Communication Skills (WOCS) by performing a step-by-step instrument validation through exploratory factor analysis (EFA).

themes.name: Motivation and attitudes assessment
themes.definition: Research that designs or validates instruments to measure engineering students' motivation, attitudes, or motivational behaviors, often in the context of capstone courses, sustainable engineering, or self-regulated learning.
evidence: [CY59SPDS] This research paper reports the quantitative validation of instruments for assessing engineering students' motivational attitudes and behaviors in their capstone design course.
[PYM3MQNK] The aims of this work were to investigate the dimensionality of the motivated strategies for learning questionnaire (MSLQ) and compare the validation of the three competing models.
[NLXE3X6S] The purpose of this study was to design an assessment instrument to evaluate students’ attitudes toward sustainable engineering (SE).

themes.name: Internship and work experience evaluation
themes.definition: Studies that adapt or validate questionnaires to assess engineering students' perceptions of their internship or work experiences, focusing on factors like workplace support, university support, and competency development.
evidence: [DFVK7NR2] The purpose of this study was to validate a newly adapted version of the Work Experience Questionnaire (WEQ), which can be used for evaluating engineering students' perception of their internship experience.

[XHXW8PNL] The purpose of this paper is to assess engineering students’ perceptions of their internship experiences. For that purpose, the validation of a recently adapted version of the Work Experience Questionnaire (WEQ) was carried out on a sample of 447 engineering students.

themes.name: Entrepreneurial mindset and design mindset
themes.definition: Research that develops or validates instruments to measure constructs related to entrepreneurial mindset (e.g., connections, creating value) or design mindset (e.g., iteration, co-evolution) in engineering students.
evidence: [K9E5C83P] This study examines the use of two survey instruments designed to measure entrepreneurial mindset (EM) constructs, such as Connections and Creating Value in engineering students.

[6XVSWITA] This article defines and operationalizes the construct design mindset and introduces the Design Mindset Inventory (D-Mindset0.1), allowing us to measure and leverage statistical analyses to advance our understanding of its role in design.

themes.name: Grit and engineering mindset
themes.definition: Studies that examine the psychometric properties of instruments measuring grit (perseverance and passion for long-term goals) and engineering mindset (iterative, failure-tolerant approach) and their relationship to academic achievement.
evidence: [PH5ZR5GA] This paper describes a twofold psychometric study on the impact of grit and engineering mindset on the academic achievement of undergraduate engineering students. Grit, explicitly the perseverance and passion for a defined long–term goal, and the engineering mindset encompassing an iterative and failure-tolerant approach to problem-solving.

themes.name: Peer and self-assessment perceptions
themes.definition: Research that explores students' perceptions of peer and self-assessment, developing questionnaires to capture dimensions such as learning, reflection, motivation, and burnout.
evidence: [DYIXSFV6] This study explores Finnish chemical engineering students’ peer and self-assessment perceptions. ... In Study II, we develop a new questionnaire for engineering students’ peer and self-assessment perceptions, as pre-existing questionnaires fail to adequately capture these dimensions.

themes.name: Competence assessment in mathematics and engineering fundamentals
themes.definition: Studies that develop or validate instruments to assess engineering students' competences in foundational areas such as mathematics, vector calculus, or basic electronics skills.
evidence: [HX8CUXK4] This article reports about our efforts to determine engineering students' competence in mathematics. ... we report the development of a large-scale instrument assessing engineering freshmen's competence in mathematics by applying Rasch analysis.

[FMII7TUT] The article presents the validity and reliability of the MICRORUBRI instrument based on rubrics, with problems applied to engineering that allow analyzing situations in real context, as well as the generation, visualization of surfaces, planes and vectors; its objective is to evaluate the development of competences in vector calculus.

themes.name: Professional responsibility and social responsibility
themes.definition: Research that adapts or validates scales to measure engineering students' professional responsibility or social responsibility, often in the context of ethics education.
evidence: [IV425BDL] This paper aims to adapt the 'Engineering Professional Responsibility Assessment (EPRA)' to Turkish culture. ... The adapted scale is a reliable measurement tool that can be used by engineering educators and researchers to make inferences about students' social responsibility levels.

data.meta_observations: The abstracts predominantly focus on the development and validation of measurement instruments for various psychological and professional constructs in engineering education, with self-efficacy and scale validation being the most frequent themes. Many studies employ factor analysis (EFA/CFA) and reliability coefficients. There is a notable emphasis on adapting existing scales to new cultural contexts (e.g., Turkey, India, Thailand, Hong Kong). Some abstracts lack explicit objectives, methods, or results, as noted in quality indicators, which may limit the depth of evidence for certain themes.
data.grounding_notes: All evidence quotes are verbatim from the provided abstracts. Article keys are from the closed set. Some themes (e.g., 'Grit and engineering mindset', 'Peer and self-assessment perceptions') are based on a single abstract, so frequency is low. The theme 'Competence assessment in mathematics and engineering fundamentals' combines two abstracts that focus on different but related foundational skills. No quotes were invented; all are directly from the text.
